Article Title: ‘TN becoming Vice City’: Stalin targets Vijay over Rs 140-crore heroin haul in Chennai
Article Text:

DMK president M K Stalin on Thursday criticised the ruling TVK government over the law and order situation and alleged narcotics smuggling in Tamil Nadu, accusing Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's administration of allowing the state to turn into a "Vice City".Reacting to the seizure of heroin worth Rs 140 crore in Chennai by the Union government's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Stalin said the central agency had been carrying out major drug busts in the state every month.In a post on X, the former chief minister recalled that the DRI had busted a narcotics network worth Rs 270 crore in Nagapattinam last month, allegedly linked to a TVK functionary. He questioned why the Tamil Nadu Police had failed to detect such large-scale drug trafficking in the state."Are they unable to catch them, or are they turning a blind eye?" Stalin asked, alleging that a state once known as a leading destination for investors had now become a "favourite destination" for methamphetamine and heroin smugglers.Stalin shares 'TVK Vice City' graphic, targets Vijay governmentAccompanying his post, Stalin shared a satirical graphic titled "TVK Vice City", modelled on the cover art of the video game Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.The graphic features illustrated portraits resembling Chief Minister Vijay and a TVK functionary against a neon-lit coastal skyline, along with images of narcotics, syringes, a laboratory setup, a crime scene outline and a silhouette of a person behind bars.It also incorporates television news clippings highlighting recent controversies, including a report on the National Commission for Women seeking an explanation from the Director General of Police (DGP) and another report dated November 9, 2026, quoting a man who alleged that he was threatened into recording a video statement.Stalin also accused the state's DGP of citing crime statistics a day earlier to divert public attention from the prevailing situation.He said merely responding to incidents by stating that "a case has been registered" was insufficient, and questioned why state agencies and the 65 special task force teams formed to curb drug trafficking had failed to apprehend smugglers.The DMK chief further alleged a continuing deterioration in law and order, citing major robberies, custodial deaths and alleged misconduct by TVK cadres."With so many issues unfolding in the Home Department under Chief Minister Vijay’s control, when will he speak if not now?" Stalin asked.The development followed a DRI operation in Chennai on Thursday, during which officials seized 70 kg of heroin worth Rs 140 crore from a vehicle during a check in Madhavaram. Two persons were arrested in connection with the seizure.
Article Summary: DMK president M K Stalin criticised the ruling TVK government over the law and order situation and alleged narcotics smuggling in Tamil Nadu. He accused Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's administration of allowing the state to turn into a "Vice City" Stalin said the central agency had been carrying out major drug busts in the state every month.

Article Title: India, Italy target €20bn trade by 2029, explore economic corridor linking Asia and Europe
Article Text:

India and Italy have set a target of raising bilateral trade to €20 billion by 2029, from €14.2 billion in 2025. The two countries also plan to set up task forces to ease business operations and explore an economic corridor linking Asia and Europe.The decisions were discussed during a meeting between Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal and Italian deputy prime minister and foreign minister Antonio Tajani in Rome on November 18, according to Italy's ministry of foreign affairs.The two sides also discussed the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), which aims to connect Indian markets with Europe through the Middle East using rail and maritime networks.Italy is looking to strengthen the role of its Mediterranean ports in the proposed corridor. Tajani identified the port of Trieste as a potential gateway for goods moving towards Central and Eastern Europe.Separately, the two countries have agreed to establish task forces in India and Italy to help businesses overcome bureaucratic and administrative hurdles. According to the Italian foreign ministry, the task forces will work to simplify procedures and facilitate trade and investment between the two countries.The Italian foreign ministry said IMEC could create new opportunities in trade, logistics and energy connectivity. For India, the proposed route could offer an additional link to European markets and help diversify supply chains.India and Italy are also exploring the establishment of an Innovation Hub in India, modelled on Italy's INNOVIT Centre in San Francisco. The proposed hub would bring together startups, businesses and research institutions to promote technology partnerships, innovation and investment.The two countries also discussed expanding cooperation in pharmaceuticals, chemicals, industrial machinery, automobiles, aerospace, agriculture and renewable energy. According to India's Press Information Bureau (PIB), sectoral discussions focused on technology transfer, joint research, electric mobility, food processing and advanced manufacturing.The meeting also covered the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA). According to the PIB, both sides welcomed the conclusion of negotiations and discussed how the pact could improve market access, boost investments and strengthen supply chains. Italy stressed the need for its early signing.
Article Summary: India and Italy have set a target of raising bilateral trade to €20 billion by 2029, from €14.2 billion in 2025. The two countries also plan to set up task forces to ease business operations and explore an economic corridor linking Asia and Europe.

AMRITSAR: As Sonia Gandhi ’s memoir,, brings renewed attention to her personal journey and family history, a Sikh man has an unusual connection to her past.Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village, and Kang is now preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum dedicated to her family and early life.Located in Lusiana, a village in Italy’s Vicenza province in the Veneto region, the house has gradually emerged as a point of interest for visitors, particularly from India. Kang has put up a board outside the property identifying it as the “Indian House, Place of Birth, 9 December 1946, Sonia Gandhi”.Kang, who lives with his wife, son and daughter in Brescia, about an hour’s drive from Lusiana, said he purchased the property in 2020 but declined to disclose its price. He said the family had decided to convert it into a museum and had now obtained the necessary permissions to take the project forward. With Sonia Gandhi’s memoir drawing public attention to her personal journey, he feels this is the right time to develop the property as a museum.“We want to meet Sonia Gandhi and her children, Rahul and Priyanka, to learn more about the family’s story and understand which personal belongings and other articles could be displayed in the museum. We want visitors to get a glimpse of her family background and early life,” Kang told TOI during his visit to Amritsar on Thursday.Born into an ordinary family in Lusiana, Sonia Gandhi’s journey has been extraordinary. Kang said her father, Stefano Maino, was a mason and building contractor, and there was little in her early life to suggest that she would one day emerge as one of the most influential women in Indian politics.From a modest Italian village, she went on to marry Rajiv Gandhi, become the wife of a Prime Minister, and eventually lead the Indian National Congress, one of the world's largest political parties. Her association with the Nehru-Gandhi family placed her at the centre of one of India's most influential political dynasties, marking a remarkable journey from a small-town upbringing to the corridors of power.Kang said the family would be delighted if Sonia Gandhi and her children visited the property. “We are proud owners of Sonia Gandhi’s house. It is their family home, and we are ready to hand over the keys whenever they wish to come,” he said, adding that people known to the family in the village were also eager to meet her.Stating that over the years, the property has become a talking point among villagers, Kang said locals immediately identify it as “Sonia Gandhi’s house” whenever they see visitors from India, particularly Sikhs, understanding that they have come to see the former Congress president’s ancestral home.The growing tourist interest has also benefited the village economy, with visitors spending money at local eateries and accommodation facilities. Several prominent residents, including politicians, had attended the house’s inauguration, he said. The family also organises a function every year on Sonia Gandhi’s birthday, he added.Kang said he spends 100 euros a month on a caretaker and pays around 1,000 euros annually in property taxes. Despite suggestions from some people to rent out the house for more than 800 euros a month or convert it into a gurdwara, the family has refused.“We do not want to rent out our prized possession or change its character. We intend to preserve it as a place associated with Sonia Gandhi’s family,” he said.Asked about Sikh hardliners who hold the Gandhi family responsible for Operation Bluestar, Kang dismissed their criticism, saying only a handful of such elements were pursuing their own separatist agenda. He maintained that the operation was a decision of the government of the day and that blaming the Gandhi family personally for it was misplaced.For Kang, the property is not merely a real estate acquisition but an opportunity to preserve a small piece of the personal history of one of India's most prominent political figures.
Article Summary: Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village. Kang is preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum dedicated to her family and early life.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle-age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests.Under the new rules, notified on November 13, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity, while older vehicles will have to undergo emission tests at shorter intervals. The revised framework also standardises PUC certificate validity for older emission categories across the country, replacing variations in testing requirements between states.The changes have been introduced through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amend Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The amendment came into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.Previously, the validity of a PUC certificate was determined primarily by the vehicle's Bharat Stage (BS) emission category. Consequently, a newly registered private car and an older commercial vehicle, despite belonging to the BS-VI category, were both eligible for a certificate valid for one year.The revised framework introduces a more differentiated approach for BS-VI vehicles. Certificate validity will now depend on two factors:The vehicle's age will be calculated from the date of its first registration.Under the earlier system, all private BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for 12 months, irrespective of their age.The revised rules introduce three validity brackets:This means owners of newer private BS-VI vehicles will have to undergo emission testing less frequently, while those with vehicles older than 10 years will face more frequent testing.Commercial BS-VI vehicles will also be subject to an age-based validity schedule, although the extension for newer vehicles will be shorter than that available to private vehicles.Previously, all commercial BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for one year. Under the amended rules:The revised schedule therefore offers longer validity to newer commercial vehicles, but retains more frequent testing requirements for older ones.The amendment also introduces a uniform testing requirement for vehicles conforming to older emission standards.Previously, BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles were generally subject to a six-month PUC certificate validity under the central rules. However, some states had prescribed shorter intervals. Delhi, for instance, already required these vehicles to undergo emission testing every three months.Under the revised framework, the validity period for all BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will be three months, irrespective of their age or category.This makes the three-month testing requirement applicable uniformly across all states and Union territories.For BS-IV vehicles, the earlier central provision allowed a PUC certificate validity of 12 months. However, certain states and areas within the national capital region (NCR) had already imposed a shorter six-month validity.The amended rules now prescribe six months as the standard validity period for all BS-IV vehicles across the country, irrespective of whether they are private or commercial.The change effectively brings the national requirement in line with the stricter timelines already followed in some regions.The amendment also clarifies how the validity period of a renewed PUC certificate will be calculated, depending on when the vehicle owner undergoes the emission test.Renewal within 10 days before expiry: If the vehicle undergoes testing within the 10 days preceding the expiry of its existing certificate, the renewed certificate will take effect from the expiry date of the previous certificate. This ensures that owners do not lose any remaining validity by renewing early.Renewal on or after expiry: If the test is conducted on or after the existing certificate's expiry date, the renewed certificate will be valid from the date of the test.PUC certificates issued before the amended rules came into force will remain valid until their respective expiry dates.Vehicle owners do not need to obtain fresh certificates immediately to comply with the revised schedule. The new validity provisions will apply when they renew their existing certificates for the first time under the amended rules.For instance, a private BS-VI car that is four years old and currently holds a one-year PUC certificate will become eligible for a three-year certificate at its next renewal. The revised validity will not automatically extend the certificate it already holds.All vehicles must have a valid PUC certificate issued by a testing centre authorised by the respective state government.Under Rule 116 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, vehicle owners are required to produce the certificate when demanded by an authorised official. Its validity can also be verified digitally through the Parivahan PUCC Portal.Under the earlier provisions, new vehicles across emission categories were exempt from obtaining a separate PUC certificate for the first year following their initial registration. However, the available details of the latest amendment do not clarify whether this exemption has been altered or retained.
Article Summary: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle- age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests. Under the new rules, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity. Older vehicles will have to undergo tests at shorter intervals.

Article Title: Delhi HC clarifies restaurants have no interim relief to levy mandatory service charges
Article Text:

What the 2025 judgment said

Why restaurant associations challenged the ban

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Thursday clarified that it has not granted any interim relief to restaurants allowing them to continue charging mandatory service charges from customers, despite an earlier judgment declaring the practice illegal.A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said no interim protection had been granted to restaurant associations against the March 28, 2025, judgment of a single judge, which upheld the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) guidelines prohibiting compulsory service charges.The clarification came after Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the government told the court that some restaurants were still making service charges mandatory for customers, contrary to the High Court's earlier ruling, ANI reported.Sharma submitted that restaurants could not continue the practice after the single judge had upheld the CCPA guidelines prohibiting hotels and restaurants from automatically adding service charges to food bills.Responding to the submission, the bench said it had not granted any interim relief to the restaurant associations in their appeals."Where is the interim relief? Where is the interim relief in their favour? We have not granted any interim prayer," Acting Chief Justice Sambre remarked.The court was hearing appeals filed by the National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) and the Federation of Hotel and Restaurant Associations of India (FHRAI) against the single judge's March 2025 judgment.On March 28, 2025, Justice Prathiba M Singh dismissed petitions filed by NRAI and FHRAI challenging the CCPA guidelines issued on July 4, 2022.The single judge ruled that restaurants cannot make service charges compulsory, even if they are mentioned on menus. Customers cannot be forced to pay such charges, which must remain voluntary.The court held that collecting service charges without a customer's consent amounts to an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. It also upheld the CCPA's authority to issue guidelines to protect consumer rights and prevent unfair trade practices, imposing costs of Rs 1 lakh on the restaurant associations.The judgment further said restaurants cannot automatically add service charges to bills. Customers must be informed that any additional payment towards service or staff welfare is voluntary.The single judge had also expressed concern over the use of the term 'service charge', observing that it could mislead customers into believing it was a government-imposed tax.In their appeals, NRAI and FHRAI argued that collecting service charges was a practice followed by the hospitality industry for more than 80 years and should not be treated as an unfair trade practice.NRAI contended that restaurants which clearly disclose service charges on their menus and inform customers before they place orders should be allowed to collect them.The association argued that service charges are not merely additional earnings for restaurants but are distributed among employees, including waiters, kitchen staff and other workers. It said the system also ensures that employees who do not directly interact with customers receive a share of the collection.The restaurant associations questioned whether the issue should be governed by consumer protection laws or labour laws, particularly when charges are clearly disclosed to customers.They also referred to judicial decisions, labour settlements and wage-related arrangements recognising service charges, including the Supreme Court's 1964 judgment in Management of Wenger & Co. v. Their Workmen.The CCPA issued guidelines on July 4, 2022, prohibiting hotels and restaurants from automatically adding service charges to food bills.The move followed consumer complaints that establishments were adding charges, generally ranging from 5% to 20%, without seeking customers' consent.NRAI approached the Delhi HC on July 18, 2022, challenging the guidelines. FHRAI later filed a separate petition raising similar objections.On July 20, 2022, the High Court stayed the operation of the CCPA guidelines while issuing notices on the petitions.The restaurant associations argued that the guidelines were arbitrary and would adversely affect the hospitality industry. They maintained that service charges were an established practice and helped ensure fair distribution of earnings among restaurant employees.They also pointed out that similar charges were collected in several countries, including the United Kingdom, Singapore, Japan and the United States.However, in March 2025, the single judge rejected their arguments and upheld the CCPA guidelines, ruling that restaurants cannot force customers to pay service charges. The associations have now challenged that decision before the Division Bench.
Article Summary: Delhi high court says it has not granted any interim relief to restaurants allowing them to continue charging mandatory service charges from customers. The clarification came after Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma told the court that some restaurants were still making service charges mandatory for customers. Sharma submitted that restaurants could not continue the practice after the single judge had upheld the CCPA guidelines.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his remarks at an event in Chicago. BJP leaders claimed that Rahul Gandhi called Indian democracy "sick". The video put out by news agencies, however, showed that he had actually described the democracy as "sacred".In a social media post on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari shared a clip of Rahul's address and termed him "leader of anti-India propaganda.""Rahul Gandhi called Indian Democracy 'sick' from foreign soil! Congress calls Indian democracy 'sick'. Rahul Gandhi has yet again proven he loves Parivar, & hates Democracy!" Bhandari said."Every time Rahul proves he is against Indian state, People of India & India's Democratic Fabric! Rahul Gandhi is Leader of Anti India Propaganda!" he added.Several BJP leaders also followed Bhandari in attacking Rahul, saying that the Congress leader was "moving towards senile mental dementia.""Rahul Gandhi himself is sick; he has been unwell for 10 years. He has developed an illness called obsessive-compulsive neurosis for the past 10 years, and now he is gradually moving towards senile mental dementia," BJP spokesperson Ajay Alok said."He has become incoherent. Look at him - he has no sense of place, time, or object. He thinks one thing in his mind, and something else comes out of his mouth. What was he even trying to say? Saying about his own mother that at every mile, Mummy used to sit in Papa's lap. Does Indian society speak like that or think like that? So, he is gradually losing his balance," he added.During an interaction with students at the University of Chicago in the US, Rahul Gandhi was asked why the opposition does not boycott elections if it believes they were being rigged.The Congress leader said Indian democracy was "sacred" to him and that he would need overwhelming evidence to even claim that it was under threat."Indian democracy is sacred. For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof," Rahul said."But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't participate in the election?' If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute. And we don't want to end the structure of Indian democracy," he said.Rahul said the opposition's strategy was to highlight alleged electoral irregularities and continue contesting elections until people realise what he claimed was the dismantling of the system."So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished," he added.BJP has repeatedly criticised Rahul Gandhi over his remarks during foreign visits, accusing him of maligning India and its democratic institutions.The latest controversy comes after Rahul raised allegations of "vote chori" during an earlier interaction at Columbia University, prompting BJP leaders to accuse him of insulting India and its democracy.Rahul was on a two-day visit to the US during which he interacted with students at Columbia University in New York on Tuesday and the University of Chicago on Wednesday.

NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant's decision to withdraw two cases from the bench headed by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah, which had expanded individual incidents of lapses on the part of authorities into pan-India judicial drives against similar illegalities, averted a potential religious controversy.The bench's Aug 4 order directing all states and UTs to remove stray animals from public places created a controversy as it is known that the majority of strays comprise cows and calves. A UP resident filed an application before the bench apprehending that the order was "capable of being implemented in a manner that may result in cows and their progeny being rounded up, transported or disposed of without regard to the special constitutional protection they are entitled to".Also Read| SC starts contempt case against lawyer for remarks against CJI The applicant said, "Cows have been worshipped and revered in Indian society since ancient times as 'gaumata', and religious sentiments of the public..., particularly the Hindu community, are gravely hurt whenever cows are slaughtered or otherwise ill-treated."He said a blanket order for the removal of strays by SC ran "the real risk of stray cattle being pushed across state borders, herded into inadequate holding pounds, or otherwise subjected to conditions violative of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960...instead of being rehabilitated through properly funded and regulated gaushalas".The CJI's decision to withdraw the cases, backed by the four most senior SC judges, was taken after they felt it was impermissible for a bench, not assigned the PIL roster, to create PIL jurisdiction for itself by expanding individual cases into pan-India exercises in violation of case-distribution discipline, which falls in the CJI's domain.SC sources said the CJI informed the senior judges there would be a general survey of cases before other benches to identify matters where the ambit had been expanded to give these a pan-India texture by converting them into PILs. A decision on allocation to appropriate benches would be taken after that, they said.One such case - Loganathan vs State of Tamil Nadu - started from the illegal construction of a ground plus one floor without a sanction plan and the failure of authorities to even notice it. The bench led by Justice Amanullah on March 25 said, "It is evident there are apparent widespread and blatant violations of building bylaws and land-use regulations. In view of the above, we deem it appropriate to examine the issue on a pan-India basis. " It impleaded municipal corporations and municipalities of capital cities of all states and UTs.

NEW DELHI: Azam Khan , former Samajwadi Party MP from Rampur and one of the most powerful cabinet ministers during the SP govt's term in UP in 2012-17, allegedly used the entire state machinery to build a private university over hundreds of acres of "illegally" occupied land, including agricultural fields and around 34 acres of enemy property.DThe ED last month attached land and buildings of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the trust running it, and estimated its market value at over Rs 1,170 crore. According to the agency's investigation and FIRs, Khan had forcefully "occupied" agricultural land from farmers in Singankhera village in Rampur to build the private university, of which he is the chancellor."Farmers were coerced through assault, unlawful confinement and threats into executing sale deeds in its favour," the ED claimed. When he was urban development minister in UP, "funds and material meant for public works were diverted to the university, govt works were executed on its private campus, and funds from contractors who had been allotted govt contracts were routed back to the trust as donations", the agency claimed.Khan held several important portfolios, including urban development, water supplies, waqf and minority welfare during 2012-17.In this period, he awarded several govt contracts to his Rampur constituency but also oversaw "demolition" of houses of tenants of waqf property. Ironically, he was then the minister for waqf and minority welfare. Funds came from several sources as 'donations' - Rs 6 crore from two Meerut-based educational entities through "political influence", Rs 23 crore from the UP govt for construction of an OBC boys' hostel and a hospital block in the university campus.Khan has over 25 FIRs filed against him in Rampur, and multiple money laundering investigations by ED. "In 2016, houses of several families in Rampur city, many of them tenants of waqf property, were demolished with bulldozers by a mob allegedly led by the then circle officer and others on the instructions of Azam Khan. The occupants were assaulted, threatened with false criminal cases, and robbed of their cash, jewellery and cattle," the ED said in one of its reports. Khan also ensured that debris of the demolished houses were used for laying the foundation of Jauhar University, the ED claimed.
Article Summary: Azam Khan was one of the most powerful cabinet ministers during the SP govt's term in UP in 2012-17. NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday said the opposition was “not ready to accept a non-democratic India”. He said opposition parties would continue to contest elections and expose alleged electoral irregularities, arguing that boycotting polls would undermine the legitimacy of the electoral process.Speaking at an event titled ‘The Iran War & India's Role in the World’ at the University of Chicago in Illinois, Rahul expressed confidence that the alleged discrepancies in the electoral system would eventually come to light.“What happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't contest elections'? If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that very minute. And we do not want to end the structure of Indian democracy,” Lok Sabha leader of opposition said.He said the opposition's strategy was to bring alleged irregularities to light and take the issue to the people rather than abandon elections.“Our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the meeting...until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished. But we do not want to break the electoral structure. Because once the opposition says that we are not going to fight elections, in the minds of the Indian people, that process becomes illegitimate.We do not want that. We are purposely not taking that step and we are confident,” Rahul said.He also made a big claim that the opposition was receiving information from within the Election Commission and suggested that the alleged irregularities would eventually lead to changes within the institution."The Election Commission itself is now giving us information from inside. So it is only a question of time before that structure collapses. Senior people in the Election Commission are now saying, 'Look, we cannot do this anymore.' So it has been a long journey," the Raebareli MP added.Asserting that the opposition would not accept “a non-democratic India”, Rahul said the parties were fighting to restore people's ability to express themselves without fear.“We are fighting that battle, and I am quite happy to say that we are winning that battle. It is only a question of time before those structures begin to give way. We are not ready to accept a non-democratic India. And it is not just the Congress party . It is the vast majority of Indians. We are going to ensure that our biggest strength, the ability of our people to express themselves without fear, is revived once again and remains our biggest strength,” Rahul said.The Congress leader also questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 general elections, citing the example of a Brazilian woman who, he claimed, had never visited India but voted 23 times in a state assembly election."If the voters were illegitimate in the 2024 election, if they did not exist, were fake voters or should not have voted, then how is that election legal? I will tell you again that a Brazilian woman who has never visited India voted 23 times in a state election in India," Rahul said.He further claimed that the Congress had suspected irregularities in the electoral process as far back as the 2014 general elections, pointing to what he described as politically inexplicable margins."Even in the 2014 election, we already believed that there was something wrong because the margins were just unexplainable politically," he said.Rahul said that even after obtaining what he considered proof of irregularities and presenting it to senior Congress leaders, they had advised him against making the allegations publicly."Even when I got the proof and demonstrated it to our political leaders in the Congress party, they said to me, 'Please don't say this.' For us, Indian democracy is sacred. For me, even to say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200 or 300 per cent proof," he said.A day before his Chicago interaction, Rahul, while addressing students and faculty members at Columbia University in New York, described India as being on the brink of an economic crisis, citing unemployment and problems in the education system."The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality. One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside, but India's got a massive unemployment problem. India's got a massive problem with its education system," former Congress chief said, as quoted by news agency ANI.His remarks drew a sharp response from the BJP, which accused the Congress leader of attacking India's image abroad and described him as a "leader of anti-India propaganda".BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari took to X and criticised Rahul's comments at Columbia University."Rahul Gandhi insults India at Columbia University! Rahul Gandhi calls India "Economic Disaster" & speaks against Indian Democracy!" Bhandari wrote.He further accused Rahul of harbouring "inherent hate for India's progress& Indian democracy", alleging that the Congress leader spoke negatively about the country whenever he travelled abroad.Drawing a comparison with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Bhandari said the PM upheld India's national interests and respected the spirit of the national flag during official foreign visits."Rahul Gandhi insults spirit of India's national flag by speaking against India democracy! Rahul Gandhi is a disaster as a responsible LOP!" he added.Rahul is on a two-day visit to the United States.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi says opposition parties will continue to contest elections and expose alleged electoral irregularities. He said boycotting polls would undermine the legitimacy of the electoral process. Rahul said the parties were fighting to restore people's ability to express themselves without fear. A major KFC franchisee in the US has filed for bankruptcy protection, citing rising costs and declining sales, after shutting dozens of restaurants this year. The company has warned that more outlets could close as it seeks to restructure its operations and exit additional leases.Tasty Chick’n LLC, which operates 75 KFC outlets and nine restaurants co-branded with Taco Bell across 10 US states, including Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, filed for bankruptcy on Monday. Court documents show that it owes about $16 million in unpaid royalties to Yum Brands Inc, KFC’s parent company.The franchisee said it sought Chapter 11 protection to prevent Yum from immediately terminating its franchise agreement. It has shut 44 locations since the beginning of 2026 and plans to use the bankruptcy process to exit more leases, according to court filings, Bloomberg reported.Chapter 11 is a form of bankruptcy in the United States that allows a struggling business, or, less commonly, an individual, to reorganise its debts and operations while continuing to stay open and operateIn a Tuesday filing, a Yum affiliate said it had been working with Tasty Chick’n for several months.However, it alleged that the franchisee’s sudden restaurant closures had significantly damaged the KFC brand, leaving it absent from some markets and weakening its presence and consumer confidence in those communities.Tasty Chick’n is at least the third major restaurant franchisee to seek bankruptcy protection in recent weeks. An operator of Outback Steakhouse restaurants filed for Chapter 11 earlier this month, also citing rising costs.In September, a major Wendy’s franchisee sought court protection while owing more than $147 million in royalties and fees to the burger chain’s corporate owner.The KFC franchisee employs more than 1,600 people, most of them full-time workers, according to court papers. It has filed customary motions seeking permission to continue paying wages and meeting other operating expenses while it operates under Chapter 11.
Article Summary: Tasty Chick’n LLC operates 75 KFC outlets and nine restaurants co-branded with Taco Bell across 10 US states. The company has warned that more outlets could close as it seeks to restructure its operations and exit additional leases.

The game is launching on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.The long gap between the two instalments has made GTA VI one of the most anticipated entertainment releases, with Rockstar building expectations through trailers, promotional campaigns and pre-release announcements.By using the franchise's return as a timeline, Modi's post draws a parallel between the evolution of the gaming series and India's development across economic, infrastructure and technology sectors over the same period.

NEW DELHI: A US district court has ordered alternative delivery of summons through Indian courts on NSA Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel. However, sources said the summons was not binding.The Clerk of the US Court has been directed to send the necessary judicial documents via international mail or courier to three district courts in Delhi - Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts.The order was issued by Judge Katherine Polk Failla of the court of Southern District of New York in a civil lawsuit filed by Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, founder of pro-Khalistan outfit Sikhs for Justice (SFJ).“The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” says an order by a US district court, seeking to serve summons on Ajit Doval and Samant Goel.The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. Article Title: 35 yrs on, a landmark moment: Forces kill Kashmir's last active local terrorist
Article Text:
Lateef Bhat carried a Rs 15 lakh bounty

Bhat refused to surrender, was killed trying to escape

SRINAGAR/NEW DELHI: Security forces killed 22-year-old Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat in a shootout outside a mosque in Kulgam district early Wednesday, ending a weeklong hunt and eliminating Kashmir's last known active local terrorist, according to J&K police.The killing marked what police described as a watershed moment in Kashmir's 35-year fight against terrorism, dealing a blow to Pakistan's efforts to project terrorist violence in the Valley as a home-grown movement. It also marked a turning point in Kashmir's counterterror campaign, with police saying local recruitment into terrorist ranks had fallen to almost zero. Home minister Amit Shah hailed the operation as a coordinated success of J&K police, Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, saying Bhat was Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley.Lateef Bhat, who carried a Rs 15 lakh bounty, was killed outside a mosque in Zangalpora village after a week-long chase across south Kashmir. His associate, Nisar, a new recruit, was killed near Larnoo bypass on Nov 16.J&K Police DG Nalin Prabhat called it a milestone in the fight against three decades of terrorism, saying local recruitment had fallen to almost zero. Only two Kashmiri youths joined LeT in the past two years, he said, adding that the force was working to dismantle the terrorist ecosystem.“We have been fighting Pakistan-sponsored terrorism for the past 35 years,” Prabhat said.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha said only a handful of foreign terrorists remained and J&K would soon be terrorism-free.Home minister Amit Shah posted on X, “Lateef Bhat was neutralised in an operation in Kulgam in the early morning hours. One of his terrorist associates, Umar Nisar, was also neutralised in Kulgam, the day before. The entire operation was marked by a very high level of synergy. The nation salutes the brave Jawans.”Local recruitment has fluctuated sharply over the years. The number fell from 54 in 2010 to 16 in 2013 before climbing to 53 in 2014, 66 in 2015, 88 in 2016 and 126 in 2017, according to security agencies. It peaked at 196 in 2018, declined to 143 in 2019 and rose again to 174 in 2020. Of those recruited in 2020, 76 were killed and 46 arrested. In 2021, 128 local youths joined terrorist groups — 73 were killed and 16 arrested.Bhat’s killing followed a cat-and-mouse chase that began after the Nov 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam, in which three personnel were wounded. Human intelligence, CCTV footage, cyber surveillance and details from a phone Bhat had dropped while fleeing helped security forces trace him.Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in Kulgam, had been wanted for the killing of a J&K police head constable in Anantnag and two migrant workers in Kulgam in July. He had escaped a shootout in Shopian in July, when his LeT associate, Zakir Ganie, was killed.Security forces cornered the duo in Kulgam on Nov 16. Nisar was killed near Larnoo bypass, but Bhat escaped, discarding his clothes to evade the cordon. He was traced to Jamia Mosque in Zangalpora Tuesday. Police cordoned off the area around 11pm.Kulgam SSP Anayat Ali Choudhary said security forces made repeated attempts to persuade Bhat to surrender, including a video call. Mosque committee members were also sent inside to convince him to lay down his arms. “We told him that he was still young and should surrender but he refused,” Choudhary said.Bhat opened fire around 3.45am Wednesday. Choudhary said forces exercised maximum restraint because Bhat was inside a mosque in the cordoned-off area. Bhat was killed outside the religious structure while attempting to escape. Unlike earlier operations, there was little local support for him.Bhat left his home in Nov 2025, prompting his family to file a missing-person report. He was recruited into LeT and its proxy, The Resistance Front. He also allegedly operated under Kashmir Revolutionary Army, an outfit used in attempts to sustain local recruitment.CRPF chief GP Singh congratulated personnel, saying: “Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather.” J&K Police posted, “You can run but cannot hide.”
Article Summary: Lateef Bhat, who carried a Rs 15 lakh bounty, was killed outside a mosque in Zangalpora village after a week-long chase across south Kashmir. Home minister Amit Shah hailed the operation as a coordinated success of J&K police, Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, saying Bhat was Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley.

NEW DELHI: SC Wednesday initiated contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for making derogatory remarks against CJI Surya Kant while appearing before his bench on Nov 16.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the erring lawyer to file his response by Jan 8 and also ordered him to appear personally before it on the next date of hearing on Jan 20.Also Read| CJI averts 'potential religious row', pulls cases from SC judge "Having perused the papers placed before us, which includes the requisite consent of the learned Attorney General for India under Section 15(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, we are prima facie satisfied that the motion made by the petitioner - Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) - for initiation of proceedings against the sole respondent / alleged contemnor for the alleged derogatory remarks referred to in the petition together with the attempt to scandalise the authority of the Court deserves to be taken forward," the bench said in its order.The controversy arose after the lawyer, aggrieved by an alleged procedural lapse in non-listing of a petition, questioned the integrity of the CJI in open court proceedings and went to extent of telling him "You cannot sit in that chair. You do not deserve. You do not have the integrity for that."Taking strong exception to the lawyer's scandalous behaviour, SCBA took the initiative to kick off the process against the lawyer.It first approached attorney general to take his consent which is needed to file a contempt petition. After getting his approval, the petition was drafted and filed and the court also showed the urgency to immediately list the case.SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai said that the court must deal with such people with an iron hand as such incidents keep happening. Article Title: Hindu population growth to fall behind other religions in India, globally: Pew Study
Article Text:
Hindu population in India to rise by 176m by 2070, but share to decline

India's changing religious composition

Hindu population growth

across regions

Fertility, migration and religious switching to shape Hindu population

Islam projected to overtake Christianity as world's largest religion

Also check:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's Hindu population is projected to increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, but Hindus are expected to account for a slightly smaller share of the country's population as Muslims continue to have higher fertility rates, according to new projections by the Pew Research Center.Despite the projected shift, Hindus are expected to continue making up more than three-quarters of India's population by 2070.The global Hindu population is also projected to grow by 199 million over the same period, reaching nearly 1.4 billion. However, as the rest of the world's population is expected to grow at a faster pace, Hindus' share of the global population is projected to decline from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070.The projections are part of a broader Pew Research Center study examining changes in the size and composition of major religious groups between 2020 and 2070. The estimates take into account differences in fertility rates, age profiles, religious switching and international migration.Pew said that although India's overall fertility rate has declined rapidly in recent decades, Muslim women continue to have more children on average than Hindu women.Combined with the younger age profile of India's Muslim population, this fertility gap is expected to increase the Muslim share of the country's population while reducing the Hindu share.India had 1.1 billion Hindus in 2020, accounting for around 95% of the global Hindu population. Nepal, with 24 million Hindus, Bangladesh with 13 million, Pakistan with 5 million and Indonesia with 4 million made up the other countries in the top five.The rankings are expected to change by 2070, with the United States projected to have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Australia is also expected to enter the top 10, ranking ninth with around 3 million Hindus, while the United Arab Emirates is projected to drop out of the list.Pakistan's Hindu population is expected to double to 10 million by 2070, although the country is projected to retain its fourth position in the global rankings.Outside India, much of the projected growth in the Hindu population is expected to come from Pakistan and the United States. Pakistan is likely to see an increase primarily through natural population growth, with births outnumbering deaths, while immigration is expected to be the main driver of growth in the US.The Asia-Pacific region, home to 99% of the world's Hindus, is projected to account for most of the community's growth over the next five decades. Its Hindu population is expected to increase by 191 million between 2020 and 2070.Hindus are projected to make up 28% of the region's population by 2070, compared with 26% in 2020.In North America, the Hindu population is expected to more than double from 4 million in 2020 to 9 million in 2070. Their share of the region's population is projected to increase from 1% to 2%.Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean are the only regions where the Hindu population is projected to decline in absolute numbers. If current trends continue, Hindus will account for less than 0.1% of the population in each of these regions by 2070.Pew's projections identify fertility, mortality, age structure, international migration and religious switching as the key factors determining changes in the size of religious groups.The global Hindu population is expected to gain more than 200 million people through natural increase between 2020 and 2070, with nearly all of this growth projected to take place in the Asia-Pacific region.Religious switching is expected to have little impact on the overall Hindu population. Pew said this is partly because Hindus have a high retention rate, with an estimated 99% of people raised Hindu continuing to identify with the religion as adults.The corresponding retention rates are 85% among Christians and 83% among Buddhists. Muslims have a retention rate of 99%, on a par with Hindus.Overall, religious switching is projected to reduce the global Hindu population by around 1 million people between 2020 and 2070, with most of the losses expected in the Asia-Pacific region.Migration, meanwhile, is expected to contribute significantly to Hindu population growth in North America, the Middle East-North Africa region and Europe. Together, these regions are projected to gain more than 8 million Hindus through migration by 2070.Asia and the Pacific is expected to record the largest migration-related losses. However, the region's gains through natural population growth are projected to far exceed the number of Hindus it loses through emigration.The Pew report also projects that Islam will overtake Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, as the Muslim population continues to grow at a faster pace.Both religions are expanding globally, but Pew attributed the faster growth of Islam largely to higher fertility rates among Muslims.“It's the babies,” said Conrad Hackett, a senior demographer at Pew, explaining that fertility rates play a much greater role in religious population growth than conversion and other forms of religious switching.During 2020-2025, the fertility rate among Muslim women stood at 3.1 children per woman, compared with 2.5 among Christian women. The average for women belonging to all other religious groups was 1.6, below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman needed for each generation to replace itself.According to Pew's latest estimates, there were 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims worldwide in 2020. The new projections indicate that the Muslim population will reach 2.57 billion by 2035, overtaking the Christian population, which is expected to stand at 2.52 billion.If current trends continue, the number of Muslims worldwide will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the Christian population is projected to remain just below 3 billion.The projections also point to significant changes in the religious composition of North America.The United States, where Christians currently account for 62% of the population, is projected to lose its Christian majority by 2065. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to make up 41% of the US population.In neighbouring Canada, Christians are projected to account for less than half of the population by 2030. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to outnumber Christians in the country.The rise in the number of people identifying with no religion is a significant factor behind the projected decline in the Christian share of the population in both countries.
Article Summary: Hindu population in India to rise by 176m by 2070, but share to decline.Islam projected to overtake Christianity as world's largest religion. Asia-Pacific region, home to 99% of the world's Hindus, is projected to account for most of the community's growth.

NEW DELHI: Security forces evacuated 27 people from Darul Uloom, an educational institution next to the mosque where top Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat was holed up. The evacuation took place before security forces launched an encounter against Lateef in Zangalpora village of Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district on Wednesday.According to officials, an officer from the Army's 9 Rashtriya Rifles volunteered to enter the adjoining seminary along with his buddy and safely evacuate 25 girl students and two teachers.Once the civilians were moved to a safe spot, troops of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles and the Special Operations Group of the Jammu and Kashmir Police launched the final assault and fired tear gas into the mosque to smoke out the terrorist.Officials asserted that the troops maintained a tight cordon to prevent his escape and exercised maximum restraint to ensure that the religious structure suffered no damage.Northern Army Commander Lt Gen Pratik Sharma, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, met troops in South Kashmir after the successful conclusion of the operation.According to officials, a search party accompanied by local civilians entered the mosque following specific intelligence inputs.They found a room on the top floor locked from the inside.When security personnel asked the occupant to come out, he opened fire, confirming that Bhat was inside. He had earlier managed to flee during an encounter in Shopian on July 8, in which another terrorist, Zakir, was killed.The operation followed a November 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam by Bhat and his associate Umar Nasir Dar, which left three personnel injured. I hope at least the Marathi people won’t object to my language!" he added.Shaina, however, denied the accusation claiming that the picture was of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar. She accused Sena (UBT) of twisting the incident to create a false narrative."Show me where I have torn or disrespected Hindu 'hruday samrat' Balasaheb Thackeray’s photograph. Deliberately twisting an incident to create a false narrative will not be tolerated. Anyone spreading defamatory claims against me will face legal action," she wrote on X."And yes, as I have said, I will tear Mani Shankar Aiyar’s photograph a thousand times over and this is what Balasaheb taught us," she added.Earlier in the day, Shinde-led Sena workers tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's book during a protest in Mumbai, demanding that publisher HarperCollins remove passages on pages 201 and 443.Addressing a press conference, Shaina accused Gandhi of insulting Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar by describing him as a "Hindutva exclusionary"."Sonia Gandhi humiliates Savarkar. She calls him a Hindutva exclusionary. But Balasaheb Thackeray always said that Savarkar is the soul of Hindutva," she said.Shaina also questioned Gandhi's delay in obtaining Indian citizenship, contrasting it with Savarkar's contribution to the freedom struggle."Sonia ji, it took you 15-plus years to even initiate the process of Indian citizenship. Savarkar gave 50-plus years of his life, not just in jail, but also for the cause of Bharat. Who are you to judge?" she said.Accusing Sonia Gandhi of attempting to rewrite history, Shaina said Maharashtra would not forgive her."We demand that HarperCollins eliminate pages 201 and 443. Savarkar spent 11 years in Kala Pani for India's freedom. Balasaheb Thackeray worshipped Savarkar," she said.She also questioned Gandhi's understanding of the RSS and its role in nation-building, as well as the sacrifices made during India's freedom struggle.
Article Summary: Shinde-led Sena workers tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's book during a protest in Mumbai. Sena (UBT) leaders accused Shinde Sena leader Shaina NC of disrespecting Bal Thackeray by tearing his photograph. Article Title: Child's spectacle power rising? Myopia may be more than just weak eyesight
Article Text:
The rise in spectacle power among children could signal a risk for myopia, which might result in future eye problems.

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

If your child's spectacle power keeps increasing, it may be more than just a change in eyesight. Childhood myopia, or short-sightedness, can involve the gradual elongation of the eyeball, increasing the risk of certain eye complications later in life, doctors warn.One common misconception among parents is that wearing spectacles makes eyesight weaker. Doctors say correctly prescribed glasses do not worsen myopia. However, ordinary spectacles correct blurred vision but do not necessarily slow its progression.Myopia allows children to see nearby objects clearly but makes distant objects appear blurred. Its development is linked to several factors, including family history, prolonged near-work activities and limited outdoor time. Mobile phones alone are not responsible, and even children who rarely use digital devices can develop the condition."An increase in the length of the eyeball, known as axial elongation, is an important aspect of myopia. Higher degrees of myopia are associated with a greater risk of certain eye problems later in life," said Dr Digvijay Singh, director, Noble Eye Care and paediatric ophthalmologist.Spending around two hours outdoors daily can help reduce the risk of developing myopia, although its ability to slow progression in children who already have the condition is less certain.Eye exercises, meanwhile, cannot reverse structural myopia or shorten an elongated eyeball. Taking breaks during reading and screen use can ease eye strain but does not treat myopia.Several options are now available to slow its progression in suitable children, including low-dose atropine eye drops, specially designed spectacle lenses and specialised contact lenses. Treatment must be tailored by an eye specialist, as results vary.Doctors also stress that children may not recognise changes in their eyesight, making regular eye examinations important even when they appear to see clearly. Follow-ups help monitor spectacle power, eye growth and response to treatment.During National Myopia Week (November 14-20), under the #ActOnMyopia campaign, specialists are urging parents to seek timely eye examinations and not dismiss increasing spectacle power as a routine childhood issue.
Article Summary: Myopia allows children to see nearby objects clearly but makes distant objects appear blurred. Development linked to several factors, including family history, prolonged near-work activities and limited outdoor time. Mobile phones alone are not responsible, and even children who rarely use digital devices can develop the condition.

Article Title: ‘Who can explain this to him?’: Rijiju tears into Rahul Gandhi over ‘dead economy’ jibe

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Thursday criticised Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on India's economy and democracy during a visit to the United States, accusing him of making “highly inaccurate statements about India” on foreign soil.Rijiju said the government would generally prefer not to respond to Rahul's comments but felt compelled to object when he made remarks abroad that, according to the minister, misrepresented the country's economic condition.“We wouldn't want to pay much attention to what Rahul Gandhi says; however, as the Leader of the Opposition, when he goes abroad and makes highly inaccurate statements about India, we feel compelled to register our objection. It is high time he mended his ways,” Rijiju said, according to news agency ANI.Reacting to the Congress leader's assessment of the economy, Rijiju cited the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, saying international institutions recognised India as the fastest-growing major economy.“The entire world acknowledges that India is the fastest-growing economy. It isn't as if we created the IMF or the World Bank; these international financial institutions themselves state that India is currently the fastest-growing major economy.Yet, Rahul Gandhi claims the economy is dead. Who can explain this to him?” he said.Rijiju also accused the Congress leader of damaging the political standing of his party and the opposition through his comments overseas.“I must say that Rahul Gandhi is only succeeding in dragging himself, his party, and the entire opposition further down. No true Indian would want a fellow citizen to go abroad and spout nonsense about their own country,” the minister said.The minister also responded to Rahul's allegations of “vote theft” and his criticism of the state of democracy in India. Rijiju argued that Rahul's ability to protest and criticise the government demonstrated the existence of freedom of expression.“He spoke about democracy—alleging 'vote theft' and claiming that democracy does not exist in India. If there were no democracy in India, how would he be able to spend his entire day protesting and hurling insults at PM Modi, the BJP, and the government? If there were no democracy, where would he get the freedom to speak from morning till night?” Rijiju said.“In India, everyone—from an ordinary individual to a political leader—is free to express whatever they wish, all day long. India operates as an incredibly open democracy; yet, despite exercising this freedom, he claims there is no democracy or freedom of speech—what exactly is he trying to prove?” he added.The BJP leader also cited figures he attributed to the IMF on poverty reduction between 2011 and 2023.“The data from the IMF reveals that between 2011 and 2023, more than 500 million (50 crore) people in India have risen above the poverty line. 500 million people have risen out of extreme poverty. In other words, India has set a record for the fastest reduction of poverty in the world,” he said.Rahul made his remarks during an interaction at Columbia University in New York on Wednesday. Speaking about unemployment and the education system, he said, “The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality. One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside, but India's got a massive unemployment problem.India's got a massive problem with its education system.”Responding to moderator Lydia Polgreen's question about young people, Rahul said many, particularly those from middle-class families with formal education, were frustrated because they did not see a clear future for themselves.The remarks have prompted a fresh exchange between the Congress and the BJP over the state of the economy, employment and democratic institutions.
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju slams Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on India's economy and democracy during a visit to the United States. The minister accused Rahul of making “highly inaccurate statements about India’s economic condition. He also accused the Congress leader of damaging the political standing of his party and the opposition through his comments overseas.

NEW DELHI: The political storm over an allegedly torn photograph of late Shiv Sena founder Bal Thackeray escalated on Thursday, with hundreds of Shiv Sena (UBT) workers taking to the streets in Mumbai to protest against Shaina NC and demand an FIR against her.The protesters, including a large number of women, gathered outside Sena Bhavan in Dadar, the headquarters of the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT), and raised slogans against Shaina.Several protesters were later detained by police, an official said.Heavy police deployment was seen outside the premises to prevent any untoward incident and maintain law and order.The protest came a day after Shaina found herself at the centre of an embarrassing episode during a political demonstration organised by the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena against Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's remarks on Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar in her memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'.During the protest, Shiv Sena leaders, including Shaina, tore copies and pages of the book to register their opposition to Gandhi's remarks. Article Title: 'Use of natural resources boomerang-ing back to bite': India accuses Pakistan of self-aggrandisement

NEW DELHI: India launched a sharp attack on Pakistan at a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) meeting, accusing its military establishment of exploiting the country's natural resources for personal gain and fomenting conflict with neighbouring countries at the expense of its own people.Speaking at an Arria-formula meeting convened by Liberia on natural resources and conflict, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, hit back after the Pakistani delegation raised the Indus Waters Treaty Harish said New Delhi had no intention of bringing bilateral issues into the discussion but was compelled to respond to Pakistan's attempt to misuse the forum."Mr. Chair, it was not our intention to bring other issues into this forum, but my delegation is compelled to respond to the comment made by the delegation of Pakistan that has chosen to misuse today's discussion to peddle its propaganda. Our position on the Indus Waters Treaty remains clear and consistent and has been articulated at multiple fora," he said.Targeting Pakistan's military establishment, Harish referred to an incident involving army chief Asim Munir, who was seen displaying a wooden case containing mineral stones to foreign leaders. He pointed out that the military's involvement in resource exploitation was also linked to political developments within Pakistan, including the removal of an elected provincial government and the imposition of a state of emergency.He said, "Their army chief was seen last September displaying a wooden box filled with mineral stones to foreign leaders, a clear indication of their army's role in this exploitation, which is also believed to be behind the recent dismissal of a provincial government in Pakistan and imposition of a state of emergency there."Last year, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir were photographed presenting rare earth minerals to US President Donald Trump at the White House. The photograph showed Munir gesturing towards an open wooden case containing the minerals, while Trump looked inside and Sharif stood nearby.The Indian envoy further lashed out Pakistan's military leadership of prioritising its own interests over the welfare of ordinary citizens and warned that its policy of fomenting conflict with neighbouring countries was hurting Pakistan itself."Pakistanis would be served well if its real rulers, its military, used the country's natural resources for the benefit of their population rather than self-aggrandisement. They would also be served better if the Pakistani army stops fomenting conflict for its neighbours, which is actually boomerang-ing back to bite their own country," the envoy said.Beyond the exchange with Pakistan, Harish outlined India's position on the responsible management of natural resources, arguing that illegal mining and smuggling can finance armed groups and prolong conflicts instead of contributing to national development.Thanking Liberia for convening the discussion, he said, "Liberia's own journey from conflict to recovery lends particular weight to this exchange."Harish called for greater reliance on existing voluntary international mechanisms rather than creating new frameworks to regulate natural resource trade. He cited the Kimberley Process, an international certification scheme aimed at preventing the trade in conflict diamonds, as an example of effective cooperation between governments, industry and civil society."Our experience is that cooperation works best when it is voluntary, consensus-based, and nationally led in an environment of friendship and goodwill. The Kimberley Process is an instructive example. By bringing together governments, industry, and civil society, it has curbed the trade in conflict diamonds while keeping legitimate trade open. As chair of the Kimberley Process in 2026, India is committed to strengthening its effectiveness and inclusiveness. Existing and tested mechanisms deserve to be fully utilised, and wherever feasible replicated, before new frameworks are contemplated," he said.Emphasising the need to ensure that local communities benefit from resources extracted from their land, Harish pointed to India's mining laws, under which companies are required to contribute towards the development of mining-affected areas.He also stressed the need to respect the distinct mandates of various UN bodies, arguing that the Security Council should focus on international peace and security, while broader issues of sustainable development and resource governance should be addressed by other institutions."As these discussions evolve, we should preserve the distinct mandates of the principal organs of the United Nations. The Security Council's responsibility is the maintenance of international peace and security. Broader questions of sustainable development and resource governance belong to the General Assembly, the ECOSOC, and other relevant bodies. The Peacebuilding Commission, given its inclusive composition, can support nationally owned efforts in this area. India stands ready to share its experience and to work with all partners towards practical, consensus-based approaches that enable natural resources to drive sustainable development and lasting peace," he said.
Article Summary: India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, hit back after the Pakistani delegation raised the Indus Waters Treaty. Harish said New Delhi had no intention of bringing bilateral issues into the discussion but was compelled to respond to Pakistan's attempt to misuse the forum.
